question: Does the answer depend on the solver path (ANK-only vs ANK+NK)?
mesh: gci_C, 603,592 cells -- COARSE, not gci_M. The historical freeze recorded in solve_s8.py was on gci_M (1,111,152 cells) on 2026-09-11 and was NOT re-run here.

attempt_1.arms: NK enabled on g83/g47/g13 at alpha 0 and 4; plus g83 with ADflow's full preconditioner (NKSubspaceSize 60, NKPCILUFill 2)
attempt_1.result: ALL bit-identical to the ANK-only production runs -- same forces to every printed digit, same iteration counts (286/196/190/159/307/195). Peak 6.9 GiB throughout.
attempt_1.why: All 286 iterations carry IterType = ANK. NKSwitchTol is 1.0e-6 and the L2 stopping target is also 1e-6, so the run terminates before the NK switch can fire.
attempt_1.finding: --no-nk has been a NO-OP on every production run at this tolerance. The campaign was ANK-only whether or not the flag was passed.

attempt_2.change: --nk-switch-tol 1e-4, so NK takes over at 1e-4 and drives to 1e-6
attempt_2.status: ABANDONED on instruction after ~77 min on the first case (alpha 0), against a ~28 min ANK-only norm.

observed_before_abandon.last_lines: Step 0.00-0.01, LinRes 1.000, rho frozen at 5.4642352155e-03 and changing only in the 11th significant figure across iterations 673-675
observed_before_abandon.reading: This is the gci_M freeze signature REPRODUCING ON THE COARSE MESH: NK engages, the Krylov solve achieves no reduction at all (LinRes 1.000), the step collapses, and the residual stops moving.

attempt_2.consequence: The freeze is NOT a mesh-size or memory effect. solve_s8.py attributes it to a lean preconditioner forced by memory at gci_M (12.7 GiB against 12.8 available). gci_C peaks at 6.9 GiB with room to spare and freezes anyway. That hypothesis is therefore not supported -- though the full-preconditioner arm at 1e-4 was never reached, so it is not yet formally refuted either.
attempt_2.data_loss: The run.log carrying this evidence was deleted while cleaning directories that had no result.json. The numbers above were extracted before deletion and are all that survives. Re-running arm C to ~700 iterations would recover it.

still_open: Whether ANK-only and a CONVERGED ANK+NK reach the same forces. Attempt 1 compared ANK against ANK. Attempt 2 never converged. The iterative-convergence verification this study lacks is still missing.
note_for_the_cloud: The documented fallback if ANK-only stalls at gci_F or gci_FF is 'restore ADflow's NK defaults'. On this evidence that fallback may not work, because NK stalls here at 6.9 GiB where memory is not the constraint.

attempt_3_preconditioner_diagnostic.setup: gci_C, g83, alpha 0, NKSwitchTol forced to 1e-4 so NK genuinely engages. 35 min cap.
attempt_3_preconditioner_diagnostic.status: Stopped by Claude Code during the third arm (pc_fill3) because the system was low on memory while idle. Two arms completed. Not a failure of the runs.
attempt_3_preconditioner_diagnostic.finding_1_preconditioner: CONFIRMED. With the project's lean preconditioner, 96 % of NK iterations achieve essentially nothing -- median LinRes 0.996, only 4 % below 0.9. With ADflow's defaults every NK iteration makes progress -- median LinRes 0.796, 100 % below 0.9 -- and the run finishes in HALF the iterations, 141 against 277. The hypothesis recorded in solve_s8.py, that the lean preconditioner forced by memory is why NK stalls, is supported. Cost of the fix: 8.0 -> 10.8 GiB, about +2.8 GiB, matching the '~2 GiB more' in CLOUD_RUNBOOK.
attempt_3_preconditioner_diagnostic.finding_2_solver_path: The answer does NOT depend on the solver path. Against the ANK-only production run (CD 201.7369, CDp 110.7943, CL -1599.0167): pc_lean differs by +0.018 counts on CD, pc_stock by -0.058. CDp differs by +0.039 and -0.046. CL by 1.1 and 0.1 counts. Part of even that is different stopping points -- the ANK-only run reached relres 9.98e-07 against 9.22e-06 and 1.17e-05 here. This is the iterative-convergence verification the study lacked, and it passes.
attempt_3_preconditioner_diagnostic.retraction: My earlier claim that 'the NK freeze reproduces on the coarse mesh' is now doubtful. That was read off a partial arm-C run showing 543 NK iterations with LinRes 1.000 and rho frozen at 5.4642e-03. pc_lean here uses the SAME settings and CONVERGED at rho 5.46e-03 -- the same value. So what I called a freeze was very likely a converged solution grinding at its floor with a useless Krylov solve, not a stall. The log that would settle it was deleted when I cleared partial directories, so this cannot be reconciled without re-running.
attempt_3_preconditioner_diagnostic.consequence_for_the_cloud: The documented fallback -- 'restore ADflow's NK defaults if ANK-only stalls at gci_F or gci_FF' -- now looks SOUND rather than doubtful, which reverses what I said earlier today. It costs about +2.8 GiB per case and halves the iteration count.

CORRECTION.what_was_wrong: I reported both arms as CONVERGED and pc_stock as 'finishing in HALF the iterations'. Both statements are false. My summary script printed the word CONVERGED whenever a result.json existed, without reading the converged flag -- PLAN 0.3, exit code 0 is not success, in my own reporting code this time.

truth.note: Neither reached the target. BOTH hit the 35 minute cap: 35:06 and 35:20.

cost_per_iteration.meaning: pc_stock did half the iterations because each costs twice as much, not because it needed fewer. In equal wall time pc_lean got FURTHER: 9.22e-06 against 1.17e-05.

CORRECTION.what_survives: The preconditioner QUALITY finding is per-iteration and stands: lean gives median LinRes 0.996 with only 4 % of Krylov solves below 0.9, stock gives 0.796 with 100 % below 0.9. The lean preconditioner really is doing nothing. It just does not follow that fixing it pays, because a working Krylov solve here costs 2x per iteration and still lost the race.
CORRECTION.what_falls: 'pc_stock halves the iteration count' and 'the NK defaults fallback now looks sound' were both over-read from a run that never converged.

why: ANK-only REACHES the target: the production gci_C alpha 0 run converges at relres 9.98e-07 in 286 iterations, about 28 minutes on this mesh.
NK with the project preconditioner: 96 % of Krylov solves achieve nothing, and after 35 minutes it is at 9.22e-06 -- an order of magnitude short.
NK with ADflow's preconditioner: the Krylov solve works, but at 1.98x the cost per iteration, and after 35 minutes it is at 1.17e-05 -- further short still, plus 2.8 GiB.
There is no accuracy argument either way: the forces agree to within 0.06 counts on CD.
At the production setting the question is moot anyway -- NKSwitchTol 1e-6 equals the L2 target, so NK never fires and --no-nk is a no-op.
recommendation.still_open: Whether ANK-only converges at 2.3M and 4.7M cells. It is proven to 1,172,856. If it stalls there, NK with ADflow's preconditioner remains the fallback to try -- but on this evidence it should be treated as unproven, not as a known-good escape hatch.
recommendation.caveat: One mesh, one geometry, one incidence, switch forced to 1e-4, and both arms truncated by a 35 minute cap rather than run to convergence. A clean answer needs them run out.
